entries.note: The README lists NoSQL injection under vulnerabilities in code. loginHandler passes req.body.username and req.body.password into User.find at routes/index.js line 52. JSON bodies are enabled in app.js, so the query document is request data.
The README lists command execution under vulnerabilities in code. create() takes a URL out of the todo body and concatenates it into child_process.exec at routes/index.js line 174.

The README lists code injection on account details: the POST body is passed through to the Handlebars view. save_account_details copies req.body to profile at routes/index.js line 104 and renders it at line 120.
The admin seed lookup at mongoose-db.js line 48 is a User.find whose username is a constant. It sits beside the login find that puts the request body into the query document.
The README lists information exposure via hardcoded values. The express-session secret at app.js line 43 is a string literal. It is a training value, not a live credential.
The same hardcoded-values note covers the token literal at app.js line 83, which line 84 writes to the log. It is a training value, not a live credential.
The MySQL connection options at typeorm-db.js line 12 set password to a literal. That is a hardcoded database credential beside the session secret, not an environment read.
mongoose-db.js lines 35-40 take the Mongo connection string from MONGOLAB_URI or MONGODB_URI. That is the environment-variable look-alike beside the hardcoded session secret and database password.
